events.title: Democratisation: closed autocracy to electoral autocracy
events.detail: Derived from a change in the Regimes of the World classification, which is itself built from V-Dem expert ratings. It marks the year a country crossed a threshold, not a specific law or decision.
events.source: derived: Regimes of the World / V-Dem
events.contested: Threshold classifications move in a single step, so the date reflects when a gradual change crossed a line rather than when it began. Read the continuous V-Dem indices alongside this to see the underlying trend.

events.title: Democratic opening: electoral democracy index rose 0.34 over 5 years
events.detail: From 0.26 in 1951 to 0.60 in 1956. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.

events.title: Inflation crossed 50% (reached 131%)
events.detail: Consumer price inflation rose from 13.7% to 131.4%, crossing the 50% threshold.
events.source: derived: World Bank consumer price inflation
events.contested: The 50% line is a convention, not a natural boundary. Official inflation statistics are also among the most manipulated numbers governments publish, so the true figure may be higher than the one recorded here.

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 14%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 2,082 to 1,780 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: Suharto resigns; Reformasi begins
events.detail: After the rupiah's collapse and mass protests, Suharto resigned, beginning democratisation, decentralisation of budget authority to districts, and central bank independence.
events.contested: Decentralisation is credited with improving responsiveness and blamed for fragmenting accountability and multiplying local rent-seeking. Both readings are supported by evidence from different districts.
